flags.detail: C5's 992/284 forced counts are asserted via inclusion-exclusion on hardcoded literals (kerchi=8, ZI=2, ZT=2) rather than an evaluated forcing criterion over the enumerated 2880 cells, despite FINDINGS.md language claiming it 'matches the incoming enumeration' -- an in-arc addendum from a fresh physics seat (2026-09-01) calls this a 'lock vacuity,' the same class as prior E27/E40 errors, though it also confirms the underlying inputs (|ker chi|=8 etc.) are separately verified elsewhere.

FINDINGS.md states I5's multiplicities were 're-verified exactly' in audit_checks.py, but the code only checks that hardcoded branching-rule dictionaries sum to the correct total dimension -- it does not independently derive the branchings from E6/SO(10)/SU(5) Clebsch-Gordan/Dynkin data, so 'verified' overstates what the arithmetic check does.

I4's 'narrowing' rests on treating the object's canonical nomination of E6/E8 as equivalent to the class-S construction's free choice of 6d type, collapsing 'the object happens to match the ADE type at its ends' into 'the object determines the type' -- a dimension/label match used as near-derivation.

The entire nomination scheme (N1 kind-exact matching) selects candidates for later data comparison purely on whether an abstract object-side quantity and an SM observable share an informal 'kind' (phase vs phase, probability vs probability) -- this is exactly a dimension/type-coincidence licence to compare, prior to any independent theoretical reason the two phases should be equal.

The choice-counting inputs to the bit-pricing (e.g. 'object set reduced to {+-2pi/3} by the banked nontriviality selector', 'targets: 2 deltas, no banked selector -> 1 bit') are informal judgment calls about which reductions count as 'structural selectors' versus 'genuine choices' -- these judgment calls directly determine which candidate wins the cap, i.e. the pricing rules are flexible enough to be tuned toward a preferred outcome even though this particular run is presented as data-blind.

The ledger's headline 'machine-checked' claim only verifies that each cited arc's arc_verdict.json contains a pre-chosen discriminating substring and says verdict=='PROVED' -- it does not re-derive or independently test any cited arc's mathematics. A citation could be textually present and phrase-matching while the underlying claim in the cited arc is wrong or later retracted, and this check would still pass.

The arc's own 'absence' claim (the relational route is the only one B307 leaves open) is retracted one arc later (B1032_across_breakings_route) as false, within the very consolidation campaign meant to prevent unswept absence claims.

The three degenerate cohomology slots (h1=3) and 'three generations' are explicitly flagged by the arc itself as a count/type match that is NOT a derivation -- the arc's own honesty about this is a positive, but the underlying identification is exactly the type-vs-value coincidence this seat is told to flag.

This arc's own self-correction narrative ('the same trap I diagnosed a paragraph earlier') recurs across a chain of at least 4 sibling arcs, all citing the same in-house hazard (a gap-measuring arc self-inflating its own coverage count) -- a repeated methodological wobble in the campaign's audit machinery itself.
